data.what_it_does: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) manufactures aircraft, helicopters, and engines for the Indian Defence Forces and civil customers, and provides repair, overhaul, maintenance, and upgrade services for these platforms.

bull.text: PAT has grown at a 16.1% 3-year CAGR with a high ROCE of 32% and zero debt, indicating strong profitability and balance sheet strength.
Operating margin expanded from 24.8% to 29.6% over three years while operating cash flow covered 1.31x of PAT, showing improving efficiency and cash conversion.
Management expects a large order pipeline of ₹90,000 crores in the next two years and ₹1,60,000-1,70,000 crores over 18 months to three years, providing revenue visibility.

bear.text: Management has repeatedly missed growth guidance, with 3-year revenue CAGR at only 7.1% versus guided 12-13% and recent quarterly growth falling short of 9-10% targets.
The current FY26 EBITDA margin guidance of 30% is tracking at 27.7% in the first quarter, suggesting potential margin pressure.

A significant portion of the order book (₹45,000 crores anticipated, ₹36,000 crores AON-approved, ₹65,000 crores future AON) remains unmaterialized with long 2-5 year timelines, creating execution risk.
